back: The output where MR = MC, so the firm cannot raise profit by changing output.

front: Finding price and profit from a table
back: Output where MR = MC; price from the AR column; profit type from AR against ATC.

front: Perfect competition: short run and long run
back: Short run: abnormal profit, normal profit or loss. Long run: entry or exit gives normal profit at minimum ATC, P = MC.
Normal profit (AR = ATC) with excess capacity; price above MC.
Abnormal profit can persist because barriers block entry; P > MC; usually not at minimum ATC.

front: When does a loss-making firm keep producing in the short run?
back: When price (AR) covers average variable cost and contributes to fixed costs.

front: Which structure is productively and allocatively efficient in the long run?
back: Perfect competition: P = MC = minimum ATC.
Abnormal profit attracts entry (supply up, price down); losses cause exit (supply down, price up).
